Mesillat Yesharim 19:10: And now I will bring you proofs for all these things from the Sages, of blessed memory, even though the matters are simple and need no supporting proof.
Mesillat Yesharim 19:11: In the chapter "Benei Ha-ir" (Megillah 27b) they said: his students asked Rabbi Zakkai, In what merit have you lived long? He said to them: In all my days I never urinated within four cubits of prayer, nor did I nickname my fellow, nor did I neglect Kiddush of the day. I had an elderly mother; once she sold the cap on her head and brought me wine for the Kiddush of the day.
Mesillat Yesharim 19:12: Behold, here is an instance of piety concerning the fine details of the commandments, for he was already exempt by law from providing wine for Kiddush, since he had none, to the point that his mother needed to sell the cap on her head — yet out of the trait of piety he did so.
Mesillat Yesharim 19:13: And regarding the honor of his fellow, that he did not even give him a nickname that was not disparaging, as the Tosafot explained there.
Mesillat Yesharim 19:14: And Rav Huna also tied bast fiber onto his garment, because he had sold his belt to buy wine for the Kiddush of the day.
Mesillat Yesharim 19:15: There too his students asked Rabbi Elazar ben Shamua: In what merit have you lived long? He said to them: In all my days I never took a shortcut through the synagogue, nor did I ever step over the heads of the holy people.
Mesillat Yesharim 19:16: Behold, these are traits concerning the honor of the synagogue and the honor of one's fellow creatures — not to step over their gathering, so as not to appear to be demeaning them.
Mesillat Yesharim 19:17: There too his students asked Rabbi Perida: In what merit have you lived long? He said to them: In all my days no man ever preceded me to the study hall, nor did I ever recite a blessing before a kohen, nor did I ever eat from an animal whose priestly gifts had not been separated.
Mesillat Yesharim 19:18: And they said further, his students asked Rabbi Nechunya: In what merit have you lived long? He said to them: In all my days I have never gained honor through the disgrace of my fellow, nor has my fellow's curse ever risen upon my bed.
Mesillat Yesharim 19:19: And they explained there: this is like the incident of Rav Huna, who was carrying a hoe on his shoulder. Rav Chana bar Chanilai came and wished to carry it for him. He said to him: If you are accustomed to carry such things in your own town, carry it; but if it means being honored through your degradation, that is not pleasant for me.
Mesillat Yesharim 19:20: Behold, then, that although it might appear that one who is honored through his fellow's disgrace is one who strives to demean his fellow so that his own honor may thereby increase, it is not fitting for the pious to accept honor even if it is their fellow himself who comes and willingly offers it, if it would be a disgrace to that fellow.
Mesillat Yesharim 19:21: And in this vein Rabbi Zeira said: In all my days I was never particular within my own house, nor did I ever walk ahead of one greater than myself, nor did I ever entertain improper thoughts in filthy alleyways, nor did I ever walk four cubits without Torah and without tefillin, nor did I ever sleep in the study hall, neither a regular sleep nor a brief nap, nor did I ever rejoice at my fellow's mishap, nor did I ever call my fellow by his nickname.
Mesillat Yesharim 19:22: Behold, then, deeds of piety encompassing all the ways we have mentioned above.
Mesillat Yesharim 19:23: And they further said, of blessed memory (Bava Kamma 30a): Rav Yehuda said, whoever wishes to be pious should fulfill the matters of Berachot — this concerns what is between him and his Maker. And some say: should fulfill the matters of Nezikin — this concerns what is between him and his fellow. And some say: should fulfill the matters of Avot, for there matters from all the categories are included.
Mesillat Yesharim 19:24: Now, acts of loving-kindness are a great fundamental for the pious person, for piety itself derives from kindness, and they said, of blessed memory (Avot 1:2): the world stands on three things, and one of them is acts of loving-kindness. And so they, of blessed memory, counted it among the things whose fruits a person enjoys in this world while the principal remains for him in the World to Come.
Mesillat Yesharim 19:25: And they further said (Sotah 14a): Rabbi Simlai expounded: the Torah begins with acts of loving-kindness and ends with acts of loving-kindness.
Mesillat Yesharim 19:26: And they further said (Yevamot 79a): Rava expounded: whoever possesses these three traits is known to be of the seed of Abraham our father — merciful, bashful, and a doer of kindness.
Mesillat Yesharim 19:27: And they said (Sukkah 49b): Rabbi Elazar said: acts of loving-kindness are greater than charity, as it is said, "Sow for yourselves according to righteousness, and reap according to kindness" (Hosea 10:12).
Mesillat Yesharim 19:28: And they further said (ibid.): in three respects acts of loving-kindness are greater than charity: charity is done with one's money, while acts of loving-kindness may be done either with one's body or with one's money. Charity is given to the poor, acts of loving-kindness both to the poor and to the rich. Charity is for the living, acts of loving-kindness for both the living and the dead.
Mesillat Yesharim 19:29: And they further said (Shabbat 151b): "and He will give you compassion and have compassion on you" (Deuteronomy 13:18) — whoever has compassion on his fellow creatures is granted compassion from Heaven.
Mesillat Yesharim 19:30: And this is simple, for the Holy One, blessed be He, measures measure for measure; and whoever has compassion and performs kindness with his fellow creatures — he too, in his own judgment, will be treated with compassion, and his sins will be forgiven him with kindness, for this forgiveness is itself justice, since it is a measure corresponding to his own measure. This is what they said, of blessed memory (Rosh Hashanah 17a): to whom does He forgive iniquity? To one who overlooks transgression against himself.
Mesillat Yesharim 19:31: And whoever does not wish to overlook the wrongs done to him, or does not wish to perform kindness, then justice dictates that he too will be treated only according to the strict letter of the law. See now, who is he, and who could possibly stand, if the Holy One, blessed be He, were to treat him according to the strict letter of the law? And King David prays and says (Psalms 143:2): "And do not enter into judgment with Your servant, for in Your sight no living being shall be justified."
Mesillat Yesharim 19:32: However, whoever performs kindness will receive kindness, and the more he increases in doing it, the more he will receive. And David used to pray according to this good trait of his — that he would strive to do good even to his enemies. This is what is written (Psalms 35:13): "But as for me, when they were sick, my clothing was sackcloth; I afflicted my soul with fasting." And he said (ibid. 7:5): "If I have rewarded evil to him who was at peace with me, etc."
Mesillat Yesharim 19:33: And included in this matter is not causing pain to any creature, even animals, and having compassion and pity upon them; and so it says (Proverbs 12:10): "A righteous man knows the soul of his animal." And there are already those who hold (Bava Metzia 32b): that the prohibition against causing pain to animals is a matter of Torah law, and in any case, at the very least, of rabbinic law.
Mesillat Yesharim 19:34: In sum: compassion and kindness must be firmly fixed in the pious person's heart forever, and his aim should always be to bring satisfaction to his fellow creatures, and not to cause them any kind of pain whatsoever, etc.
Mesillat Yesharim 19:35: The second component of piety is in the manner of performance, and this too is included under two headings, though many particulars are included beneath them; and the two primary ones are fear and love, the two pillars of true service, without which it cannot stand at all.
Mesillat Yesharim 19:36: Included in fear are: submission before Him, blessed be He; shame in approaching His service; and the honor given to His commandments, to His Name, blessed be He, and to His Torah.
Mesillat Yesharim 19:37: And included in love are: joy, cleaving, and zealousness. Let us now explain them one by one.
Mesillat Yesharim 19:38: Behold, the essence of fear is the fear of His grandeur, which a person must bear in mind while praying or performing a commandment — that it is before the King of kings of kings that he is praying or performing that deed. This is what the Tanna warned (Berachot 28b): "and when you pray, know before whom you are praying."
Mesillat Yesharim 19:39: Now, there are three things a person must contemplate and reflect upon well, in order to attain this fear: the first, that he is truly standing before the Creator, blessed be His Name, and conversing with Him, even though the eye of man does not see Him. And you will see that this is the most difficult thing to form as a true image in a person's heart, since the senses give no assistance to it at all.
Mesillat Yesharim 19:40: However, whoever possesses sound understanding can, with a little reflection and attention, fix in his heart the truth of the matter — how he comes and truly converses with Him, blessed be He, and pleads before Him, and requests from Him, and He, blessed be His Name, listens to him and attends to his words, just as one man speaks to his fellow and his fellow attends and listens to him.
Mesillat Yesharim 19:41: And once he has fixed this in his mind, he must reflect on His grandeur, blessed be He — that He is exalted and lofty above all blessing and praise, above every kind of perfection that our thought can conceive and understand.
Mesillat Yesharim 19:42: And further, he must reflect on man's lowliness and inferiority, on account of his materiality and coarseness, all the more so on account of the sins he has committed throughout his life.
Mesillat Yesharim 19:43: For in view of all this, it is impossible that his heart should not tremble and quake while he speaks his words before Him, blessed be He, mentioning His Name and seeking to find favor with Him. This is what Scripture says (Psalms 2:11): "Serve the Lord with fear, and rejoice with trembling." And it is written (ibid. 89:8): "A God feared in the great council of the holy ones, and awesome above all who surround Him."
Mesillat Yesharim 19:44: For the angels, being closer to Him, blessed be He, than the sons of the material body, find it easier to conceive the praise of His greatness, and therefore His awe is upon them even more than it is upon the sons of man; and indeed King David, peace be upon him, used to praise, saying (ibid. 5:8): "I will bow down toward Your holy Temple in fear of You." And it is written (Malachi 1:6): "where is My fear?" And it says (Ezra 9:6): "O my God, I am ashamed and blush to lift up my face to You, my God."
Mesillat Yesharim 19:45: However, this fear must first grow strong in the heart, and afterward its effects will be seen also in the limbs of the body — namely: the bowing of the head, prostration, the lowering of the eyes, and the folding of the hands, like a lowly servant before a great king. And so they said in the Gemara (Shabbat 10a): Rava would clasp his hands and pray, saying: like a servant before his master.
Mesillat Yesharim 19:46: Now, we have spoken up to now of submission and of shame; let us now speak of the matter of honor.
Mesillat Yesharim 19:47: Behold, the honor and preciousness due to a commandment — our Sages, of blessed memory, have already warned us concerning it, saying (Bava Kamma 9b): "This is my God, and I will glorify Him" (Exodus 15:2) — beautify yourself before Him in the performance of commandments: a beautiful tzitzit, beautiful tefillin, a beautiful Torah scroll, a beautiful lulav, etc. And they likewise said: beautification of a commandment extends up to one-third additional expense — up to this point it is from his own funds, beyond this point it is from the Holy One, blessed be He. Behold, the clear intent of their words, of blessed memory, is that it is not enough merely to perform the commandment; rather, one must honor it and beautify it.
Mesillat Yesharim 19:48: And this is to exclude one who, to be lenient with himself, would say: honor matters only to human beings, who are enticed by such vanities, but the Holy One, blessed be He, does not concern Himself with this, for He is exalted above such things and elevated beyond them, and since the commandment is performed in truth, that is enough.
Mesillat Yesharim 19:49: However, the truth is that the Master, blessed be He, is called "the God of glory" (Psalms 29:3), and we are obligated to honor Him, even though He has no need of our honor, and our honor is not significant or treasured before Him.
